title: Pet Portrait Photography (Studio Style)
description: Professional pet portrait photography style. Use for pet brand marketing, vet clinic decor, and animal shelter promotional content.

prompt.main: professional pet portrait photograph of a golden retriever sitting in a studio, soft seamless grey background, gentle catchlight in the eyes, shallow depth of field focused on the eyes, warm studio lighting, canon RF 85mm f/1.2 --ar 1:1 --v 6.1 --s 500
prompt.negative: --no cartoon, illustration, multiple dogs, leash, person

explained.why: Mid stylize balances realism and warmth. Too low = stock photo; too high = illustrated.

tutorial.intro: Pet portraits work because of eye focus + catchlight + soft background. Generic "dog photo" gets you 1000 stock results.
steps: Subject: golden retriever sitting in a studio — specific breed + pose.
Background: soft seamless grey background — studio backdrop = professional look.
Eyes: gentle catchlight in the eyes — the sparkle in the eyes is the soul of the photo.
Focus: shallow depth of field focused on the eyes — the eye must be tack sharp.
Camera: canon RF 85mm f/1.2 — real lens = real photo feel.
tutorial.tips: Catchlight = the white sparkle in the eye. Without it, even good photos look "dead".

faq.q: Why does my dog look photoshopped?
faq.a: You forgot the catchlight. "Catchlight in the eyes" is the single most important word for animal portraits.
85mm f/1.2 or f/1.4. These are the classic portrait lens focal lengths.

faq.q: How to make it look professional?
faq.a: Soft seamless background + studio lighting + catchlight. These three = "I paid a photographer".
